frequency_question: What proportion of substantive bilateral water treaty renewals in South Asia successfully meet all formal signing and documentation criteria before the expiration or within the sunset window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal inter-governmental water resource treaty negotiations between India and its coterminous neighbors (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan) where a prior treaty was up for renewal or replacement. Excludes internal water disputes or non-treaty technical committees.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty implementation and modifications (Pakistan)
Teesta River interim water sharing agreement drafts (Bangladesh)

coverage_note: 4 major bilateral water treaty negotiations identified in South Asia involving India since 1960; 3 resulted in formal signed treaties meeting strict criteria, 1 stalled prior to formal signature.
known_gaps: Minor localized sub-basin arrangements (e.g., specific Kushiyara River MOU in 2022) are omitted to focus on major basin-level successor treaties.
skeleton: Total historical bilateral water treaties attempted vs those that successfully reached formal signed text published via official government press releases within the designated timeframe.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 4 documented major attempts = 75 percent baseline criteria satisfaction rate given substantive engagement.
validity_reason: Bilateral hydropolitical frameworks evolve slowly; regional diplomatic patterns remain stable across multi-decade horizons.
